title: company sync kickoff + Q&A scratch
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratch for the company sync kickoff + Q&A. Draft talking bullets, likely hard Qs and brief answers, and reminders for follow-ups. Not polished; notes to self.

Topline (1 sentence): Redwood is doubling down on predictable inference — shipping tools and options that let product teams choose the right tradeoffs between latency, cost, and control.

Key messages (short bullets):
- Customers want reliable, cost-efficient inference; we deliver via Hosted, Dedicated, Private.
- Recent wins: Dedicated pilot onboarding (3 customers), 20% median token cost reduction from Optimize beta.
- What’s next: Private GA (regional VPC), rollout of improved KV cache heuristics, and a new fallback routing policy.
- Ask of the company: keep iterating on observability fixes and document common troubleshooting flows (SRE + Eng).

Slide order / talking flow (for my 7 min):
1) Quick context: why inference economics matter (1 min)
2) Wins (1.5 min)
3) Upcoming launches & impact (2 min)
4) Ask + operational readiness (1 min)
5) Q&A kickoff (1.5 min)

Speaker bullets (short):
- "We measured customer workloads and the biggest gaps are predictable latency and cost transparency."
- "Hosted is best for speed to value; Dedicated gives throughput predictability; Private addresses compliance and data locality."
- "Optimize reduced typical per-token spend by ~20% in beta; next step: expand quantization suggestions for medium-length contexts."

Likely hard Qs and suggested answers (scratch):
Q: "Are we going to open-source serving runtime?"
A: Emphasize tradeoffs: community builds are great; our priority is a stable, commercially supported runtime that integrates with our orchestration and observability. Open-source parts of SDK / examples are possible — escalate to legal/ops for policy.

Q: "What if Dedicated customers need custom models or libs?"
A: We support model pinning and allow vetted custom artifacts in Dedicated; Private customers can run fully on-prem. For edge cases, we offer professional services to onboard.

Q: "How does this affect token pricing?"
A: No immediate hosted price change. Optimize and Dedicated provide levers to reduce unit cost for customers. We’ll share benchmarks in the console.

Tough scenario scripts (for Qs about outages / fallbacks):
- If asked about a recent incident: be factual, timeline-based, highlight root cause work, and immediate mitigations. No finger-pointing.
- If asked about SLA: reaffirm current SLA targets for Dedicated and path to exportable reports. Point to SRE lead for deeper dive.

Phrasing to avoid (notes to self):
- Don’t overpromise dates for Private GA; use "targeting" and "Q2/Q3" windows.
- Avoid deep implementation detail (kernel/compilation) unless asked by Eng folks.

Unresolved bits (need answers before final script):
- Exact % token cost reduction to cite for Optimize (confirm with analytics).
- Final Dedicated pilot customer count and anonymized quotes.
- Legal signoff on any line about open-sourcing runtime components.

Logistics / coordination checklist:
- Ping product-marketing for one-pager (due 2026-03-11) -> @marketing lead (Slack).
- Ask SRE to prepare 1-slide incident TL;DR (due 2026-03-10) -> @sre-lead.
- Prep fallback slide for outages + contact matrix (ops).

Notes to self (style):
- Keep energy high, short anecdotes better than numbers-heavy slides.
- End with a clear "what we need" (two asks max).

Linked artifacts/refs (tickets I need):
- INF-3421 (Dedicated pilot onboarding)
- CON-550 (Optimize cost analysis)

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm Optimize metric with analytics (owner: Elena)
- [ ] Grab anonymized Dedicated pilot quote (owner: AE)
- [ ] Run talk through with product marketing (quick dry run 2026-03-11 11:00 PDT)

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Consider a small customer video clip in the comms (30s) showing latency improvement — low effort, high impact.
- Add a follow-up office hours sign-up link in the Slack announcement for deeper technical Q&A.

End of scratch.
